notes: The report commit sits on top of head_sha on the same branch; head_sha is the last implementation commit.
Every existing overworld golden hash is byte identical to base_sha. This was verified after each integration by diffing the fixture entries, which reported OVERWORLD_ENTRIES_SAME True.

The six nether golden entries are new. They were re-pinned once, when the decoration pass moved inside generateChunk, with golden:update touching only the netherEntries block (6 insertions, 6 deletions).

Nether chunk generation is 6.452 ms on a quiet runner, just above the 6 ms bench maximum but far inside the suite assertion of bench maximum times failFactor. The H-06 budget item was the overworld average, which is now 2.193 ms. The remaining nether cost is the 3D cave noise; memoising the perlin3Raw gradients is the next step.

The frozen caveThreshold 0.42 is compared against an amplified fbm3 value. A local non frozen constant NETHER_NOISE.amplitude 4.5 in packages/world scales the normalised noise, because the raw normalised fbm3 never reaches 0.42 and no cave would ever open. No frozen value was changed.

Decoration rates measured over many chunks: quartz 0.170 and 0.172 against the frozen 0.18 because veins are column local, soul sand about 0.194 because magma rolls first, magma about 0.09 globally because the chance tapers with height away from the lava shore, glowstone exactly 2 clusters per chunk.

Village decoration runs after vegetation inside a chunk, so a tree that spills across a chunk border can overwrite a village voxel depending on chunk visit order. The village pass itself is order independent and is covered by its own suite; the wiring suite asserts presence rather than exact order independence.

PORTAL.lightLevel 11, PORTAL.travelDelayTicks 80 and PORTAL.cooldownTicks 300 are not consumed by packages/world. They belong to whoever owns portal block light emission and travel timing in sim or gameplay. No shared contract change is requested.

Only packages/world and this report file were touched. The four L2 children worked in their own clones of the same environment, created no environments, and all their work was integrated by L1-F on this branch.
